subject: HEALTH
title: Health 4
description: Grade 4 health education aligned to the 2008 California Health Education Content Standards, which focus fourth grade on Nutrition and Physical Activity and on Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs. Students learn nutrients and MyPlate, read Nutrition Facts labels, plan balanced meals and snacks, practice food safety, and set physical-activity goals; then they study safe medicine use, the effects of tobacco/vaping and alcohol, influences such as advertising and peers, and refusal and decision-making skills, finishing with a family health-promotion campaign.
framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grade 4: Nutrition and Physical Activity; Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs); 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.H-4.1.1.N: Identify the key nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water) and their functions.
standards.H-4.1.2.N: Describe the food groups and the recommended daily amounts from each (MyPlate).
standards.H-4.1.3.N: Explain the benefits of eating a healthy breakfast and a variety of fruits and vegetables.
standards.H-4.1.4.N: Explain the importance of drinking water and limiting sugar-sweetened beverages.
standards.H-4.1.5.N: Describe the benefits of daily physical activity and the recommended 60 minutes per day for children.
standards.H-4.1.6.N: Explain safe food handling and storage practices.
standards.H-4.2.1.N: Describe internal and external influences (family, culture, media, advertising) on food choices and physical activity.
standards.H-4.3.1.N: Use the Nutrition Facts label to locate valid information about foods.
standards.H-4.4.1.N: Practice effective communication to ask for healthy food and activity options at home and in the community.
standards.H-4.5.1.N: Use a decision-making process to choose healthy foods and snacks.
standards.H-4.6.1.N: Set a short-term goal to improve nutrition or increase physical activity and track progress.
standards.H-4.7.1.N: Plan a nutritious meal and snack using MyPlate.
standards.H-4.7.2.N: Track daily food intake and physical activity.
standards.H-4.8.1.N: Encourage others to make healthy food and physical activity choices.
standards.H-4.1.1.A: Identify safe and unsafe uses of medicines; distinguish prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
standards.H-4.1.2.A: Describe the short- and long-term effects of tobacco and nicotine use, including e-cigarettes/vaping and secondhand smoke.
standards.H-4.1.3.A: Describe the short- and long-term effects of alcohol use.
standards.H-4.1.4.A: Recognize that most young people do not use alcohol, tobacco or other drugs (social norms).
standards.H-4.1.5.A: Identify dangers of inhalants and household poisons.
standards.H-4.2.1.A: Analyze how advertising and the media influence decisions about alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-4.2.2.A: Describe how family and peers influence choices about alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-4.3.1.A: Identify trusted adults and community resources for help with alcohol, tobacco and other drug concerns.
standards.H-4.4.1.A: Demonstrate refusal skills to avoid alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-4.5.1.A: Use a decision-making process to avoid alcohol, tobacco and other drug use.
standards.H-4.6.1.A: Set a personal goal to remain alcohol-, tobacco- and drug-free.
standards.H-4.7.1.A: Practice safe use of medicines (read labels, take only with adult supervision).
standards.H-4.8.1.A: Encourage others to be alcohol-, tobacco- and drug-free.

units.title: Health Skills and Wellness
units.big_idea: Good health comes from everyday choices and skills we can practice.

units.title: Nutrients and MyPlate
units.big_idea: Our bodies need a variety of nutrients from every food group.

units.title: Food Labels and Influences
units.big_idea: Labels give reliable information, while ads and habits influence what we choose.

units.title: Planning Healthy Meals and Food Safety
units.big_idea: Balanced meals and safe food handling keep families healthy.

units.title: Physical Activity for Life
units.big_idea: Sixty minutes of daily activity strengthens the heart, muscles and mind.

units.title: Medicines and Household Safety
units.big_idea: Medicines help when used correctly; unsafe use and poisons can harm.

units.title: Tobacco and Vaping
units.big_idea: Nicotine is addictive and harms the body; most young people choose not to use it.

units.title: Alcohol
units.big_idea: Alcohol affects the brain and body and is especially harmful to growing kids.

units.title: Influences, Decisions and Refusal Skills
units.big_idea: Recognizing influences and practicing refusal skills helps us stay drug-free.

units.title: Health Promotion Campaign
units.big_idea: We can encourage our families and communities to make healthy choices.

objectives: Describe physical, mental and social health

days.title: Health triangle
days.work: Draw a health triangle (physical, mental/emotional, social) and list 3 habits for each side.

days.title: Habit inventory
days.work: Complete a 15-item checklist of daily habits (sleep, water, activity, fruits and vegetables) and circle strengths.

days.title: Health journal
days.work: Set up a health journal and write about one healthy habit your family already has.

days.title: Healthy day schedule
days.work: Plan an ideal healthy day schedule with meals, activity, screen time and 9-12 hours of sleep.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Share the health triangle with family and answer 5 quick-check questions on health dimensions.

days.title: Decision steps
days.work: Learn a decision model (Stop, Think of options, Consider consequences, Choose, Check) and apply it to a snack choice.

days.title: Scenario practice
days.work: Work through 3 scenarios (skipping breakfast, choosing an after-school activity, drink at a party) with the model.

days.title: SMART goals
days.work: Rewrite 4 vague goals ('eat better') as SMART goals.

days.title: Your goal
days.work: Write a personal 2-week SMART goal for eating or activity and make a tracking chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain your decision-making steps to a parent using a real choice from today.

days.title: Trusted adults
days.work: Make a 'helping hand' tracing listing 5 trusted adults and how to reach them.

days.title: Reliable vs unreliable
days.work: Compare a health ad with a KidsHealth article and list clues that show which is reliable.

days.title: Asking for help
days.work: Role-play asking a trusted adult for help with a health question.

days.title: Health helpers
days.work: Identify community health helpers (school nurse, pharmacist, doctor, poison control 1-800-222-1222).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a quiz on reliable sources and trusted adults; check your goal tracker.

days.title: Nutrient jobs
days.work: Learn what carbohydrates, proteins and fats do and make a 3-column chart.

days.title: Food sort
days.work: Sort 20 food pictures or packages by their main macronutrient.

days.title: Whole grains
days.work: Compare white and whole-wheat bread labels and explain why whole grains give longer-lasting energy.

days.title: Healthy fats
days.work: Learn the difference between fats in avocados and nuts and fats in fried foods.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on macronutrients and their functions.

days.title: Vitamins and minerals
days.work: Research one vitamin and one mineral (e.g., vitamin C, calcium) and their sources and jobs.

days.title: Water's job
days.work: Learn how water regulates temperature and track your water intake for one day.

days.title: Sugar in drinks
days.work: Measure the teaspoons of sugar in a soda, juice drink and sports drink using labels and compare.

days.title: Rethink your drink
days.work: Make a chart of healthier drink swaps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write 3 reasons water is the best drink choice.

days.title: MyPlate
days.work: Label a paper plate with the 5 MyPlate food groups and recommended proportions.

days.title: Food group collage
days.work: Cut magazine pictures and glue them into the correct food groups.

days.title: Portions
days.work: Measure portion sizes of cereal, milk and fruit and compare to what you usually eat.

days.title: Cultural foods
days.work: Identify food groups in 3 cultural dishes (tamales, stir-fry, pasta).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on food groups and amounts.

days.title: Breakfast power
days.work: Read about how breakfast fuels the brain and list 5 quick healthy breakfasts.

days.title: Make breakfast
days.work: Prepare a healthy breakfast with 3 food groups.

days.title: Eat the rainbow
days.work: Track the colors of fruits and vegetables you eat for 3 days.

days.title: Taste test
days.work: Taste-test 3 new fruits or vegetables and rate them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph about the benefits of breakfast and fruits and vegetables.

days.title: Food log day 1
days.work: Record everything you eat and drink today in a food log by food group.

days.title: Food log day 2
days.work: Continue the food log and add activity minutes.

days.title: Food log day 3
days.work: Complete the third day of the log.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Compare your 3-day log to MyPlate and identify one food group to increase.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 2 test on nutrients and MyPlate.

weeks.assessment: Food log analysis and Unit 2 test.

objectives: Locate key information on the Nutrition Facts label
Use % Daily Value to compare foods

days.title: Label parts
days.work: Label a printed Nutrition Facts panel: serving size, calories, fat, sodium, fiber, added sugars and % Daily Value.

days.title: Serving size
days.work: Compare the serving size to the whole package on 3 snacks and calculate how many servings each package holds.

days.title: 5/20 rule
days.work: Learn the 5/20 rule (5% DV or less is low, 20% or more is high) and mark 'low' and 'high' nutrients on 3 labels.

days.title: Pantry scavenger hunt
days.work: Find the cereal or snack in the pantry with the most fiber and the least added sugar and record the numbers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a label-reading quiz using a new food package.

objectives: Use labels and a decision model to choose snacks

days.title: Whole vs processed
days.work: Compare an apple, applesauce and an apple-flavored fruit snack label and rank them by nutrients.

days.title: Snack decision
days.work: Use the decision model to choose an after-school snack from 4 options and explain the choice.

days.title: Sodium check
days.work: Compare sodium in chips, pretzels, popcorn and nuts and graph the results.

days.title: Make a snack
days.work: Prepare a nutrient-dense snack (veggies and hummus, yogurt parfait) and list its food groups.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a 'Snack Smart' guide with 5 tips and 5 snack ideas.

objectives: Analyze how food ads target kids
materials: recorded TV or online food ads

days.title: Ad detectives
days.work: Watch 3 food commercials and record techniques used (cartoons, prizes, celebrities, catchy songs).

days.title: Cereal box analysis
days.work: Compare the front of a sugary cereal box with its Nutrition Facts label and note what the front leaves out.

days.title: Influences web
days.work: Make a web of influences on your food choices: family, culture, friends, media, cost, taste.

days.title: Create an ad
days.work: Design a cereal box or poster that advertises a healthy food using the same techniques honestly.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on how ads try to influence kids and how to think critically about them.

days.title: I-messages
days.work: Practice I-messages to ask for healthy food ('I feel more energy when we have fruit at breakfast; could we buy berries?').

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Role-play asking for a healthy option at a restaurant, a friend's house and the grocery store.

days.title: Family traditions
days.work: Interview a family member about a traditional family dish and identify its food groups.

days.title: Healthy twist
days.work: Suggest one healthy twist to the family recipe and discuss it with the cook.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 3 test on labels, influences and communication.

objectives: Plan a balanced meal and snack using MyPlate

days.title: Meal analysis
days.work: Analyze 3 sample dinners and decide which food groups are missing.

days.title: Plan a dinner
days.work: Plan a family dinner that includes all 5 food groups.

days.title: Budget
days.work: Use a grocery flyer to price the ingredients and stay within a $20 budget.

days.title: Snack plan
days.work: Plan two healthy snacks for the week.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the menu to family and explain how it follows MyPlate.

days.title: Kitchen safety
days.work: Learn kitchen safety rules (handwashing, knife safety with adult, hot surfaces).

days.title: Shop
days.work: Help shop for the meal planned last week, reading labels to choose items.

days.title: Prep
days.work: Wash and prepare vegetables with adult help.

days.title: Cook
days.work: Cook the planned dinner with an adult and measure ingredients.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a reflection: what food groups were in the meal and how did it taste?

objectives: Explain safe food handling and storage

days.title: Clean
days.work: Use glitter on hands to model germ spread, then practice 20-second handwashing.

days.title: Separate
days.work: Learn why raw meat stays separate from produce and sort grocery items for safe storage.

days.title: Cook
days.work: Learn safe cooking temperatures and check one with a food thermometer.

days.title: Chill
days.work: Check the refrigerator temperature (40°F or below) and list leftovers rules.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a Clean-Separate-Cook-Chill poster for the kitchen.

objectives: Make healthy choices when eating out

days.title: Menu choices
days.work: Read a restaurant kids' menu and choose a balanced meal and drink.

days.title: Portions out
days.work: Compare restaurant portion sizes with MyPlate recommendations.

days.title: Fast food swaps
days.work: Find 3 healthier swaps at a fast-food restaurant using online nutrition info.

days.title: Family meal
days.work: Plan a screen-free family meal with conversation questions.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 4 test on meal planning and food safety.

days.title: Benefits
days.work: List physical, mental and social benefits of physical activity.

days.title: Activity types
days.work: Sort activities into aerobic, muscle-strengthening and bone-strengthening.

days.title: Heart rate
days.work: Measure heart rate before and after 3 minutes of jumping.

days.title: Mood check
days.work: Rate your mood before and after a 15-minute walk.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on activity guidelines and benefits.

days.title: Activity log
days.work: Log activity minutes for 3 days.

days.title: Screen time log
days.work: Log screen time for the same 3 days.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare activity to the 60-minute goal and screen time to family limits.

days.title: Swap
days.work: List 5 active alternatives to screen time.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write what you learned from your logs.

objectives: Set and track a physical-activity goal

days.title: Barriers
days.work: List barriers to being active (weather, time, screens) and a solution for each.

days.title: Set goal
days.work: Write a 3-week SMART activity goal (e.g., 30 minutes of outdoor play after school 5 days a week).

days.title: Activity menu
days.work: Create an 'activity menu' of indoor and outdoor choices for rainy and sunny days.

days.title: Track
days.work: Begin tracking the goal on a calendar with stickers and note how you feel each day.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Check progress after 5 days and adjust the plan if needed.

days.title: Family challenge
days.work: Design a one-week family activity challenge with daily tasks (walk after dinner, dance party).

days.title: Lead activity
days.work: Lead the family in a 15-minute active game you choose.

days.title: Advocacy poster
days.work: Make a poster encouraging 60 minutes of play a day for kids in your neighborhood.

days.title: Goal check
days.work: Review your 3-week goal tracker and reflect on progress.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 5 test on physical activity.

days.title: Why medicines?
days.work: List reasons people take medicines (treat illness, prevent disease, relieve pain) and the risks of misuse.

days.title: Rx vs OTC
days.work: Compare a prescription label and an OTC drug facts label in a Venn diagram.

days.title: Health helpers
days.work: Learn the roles of doctors and pharmacists; write 3 questions you could ask a pharmacist.

days.title: Not candy
days.work: Discuss why some medicines look like candy and why only adults should give medicine.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on types of medicines and who can give them.

objectives: Read medicine labels for safe use
materials: OTC medicine box (empty or with adult)

days.title: Drug Facts label
days.work: With an adult, find active ingredient, uses, warnings, directions and expiration date on a Drug Facts label.

days.title: Side effects
days.work: Learn what side effects are and why you tell an adult if you feel unwell after medicine.

days.title: Safe rules
days.work: Write 5 safe medicine rules (only from a trusted adult, never share prescriptions, follow dose).

days.title: Scenario practice
days.work: Act out what to do if a friend offers you a pill or you find medicine on the floor.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a safe medicine checklist and explain it to a younger sibling or parent.

days.title: Poison hunt
days.work: With an adult, find 10 household products with warning labels and note signal words (Caution, Warning, Danger).

days.title: Inhalants
days.work: Learn why sniffing fumes from products like markers, glue or aerosols harms the brain and can be deadly.

days.title: Safe storage
days.work: Help organize cleaning products out of reach and away from food.

days.title: Poison Control
days.work: Learn the Poison Control number (1-800-222-1222) and role-play calling it.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 6 test on medicines and household safety.

objectives: Describe short- and long-term effects of tobacco

days.title: What's in tobacco
days.work: Learn about nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide and what each does to the body.

days.title: Lung model
days.work: Model healthy vs smoker's lungs by soaking one sponge in dark syrup and comparing.

days.title: Straw breathing
days.work: Jog in place, then breathe through a straw for 30 seconds to feel restricted breathing (stop if dizzy).

days.title: Addiction
days.work: Read how nicotine causes addiction and why quitting is hard.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a body diagram labeling 6 effects of tobacco.

days.title: What is vaping?
days.work: Read an FDA fact sheet on e-cigarettes and list what is in the aerosol.

days.title: Myth or fact
days.work: Sort 10 statements about vaping into myth or fact.

days.title: Flavors and marketing
days.work: Analyze how flavors and colorful packaging target young people.

days.title: Brain effects
days.work: Learn how nicotine affects the developing brain.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a public service message correcting one vaping myth.

objectives: Recognize that most youth do not use tobacco

days.title: Secondhand smoke
days.work: Learn how secondhand smoke and vape aerosol affect others, especially children.

days.title: Smoke-free laws
days.work: Read about California's smoke-free laws for restaurants, parks and cars with kids.

days.title: Social norms data
days.work: Read survey data showing most California students have never used tobacco and graph it.

days.title: Avoiding smoke
days.work: List ways to avoid secondhand smoke politely.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 7 test on tobacco and vaping.

objectives: Describe short- and long-term effects of alcohol

days.title: What is alcohol
days.work: Learn what alcohol is and why it's illegal for people under 21.

days.title: Short-term effects
days.work: List short-term effects (slowed reaction time, poor balance, poor judgment).

days.title: Coordination demo
days.work: Walk a tape line while spinning first to feel how impaired balance makes tasks hard; discuss.

days.title: Long-term effects
days.work: Learn long-term effects on liver, heart and brain.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Label a body outline with effects of alcohol.

objectives: Explain why alcohol is more harmful to young people

days.title: Brain parts
days.work: Label brain parts and their jobs (thinking, memory, balance).

days.title: Growing brain
days.work: Read why young brains are more affected by alcohol.

days.title: Norms
days.work: Read data showing most young people don't drink alcohol.

days.title: Safety
days.work: Discuss drunk driving and what to do if an adult who has been drinking offers you a ride.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write 3 reasons kids choose not to drink.

weeks.topic: Family rules and influences about alcohol

days.title: Family interview
days.work: Interview a parent about family rules on alcohol, tobacco and medicine and why they exist.

days.title: Influences
days.work: List positive and negative influences from family, friends and media.

days.title: Trusted adults
days.work: Review trusted adults you can talk to about alcohol or drug concerns.

days.title: Family agreement
days.work: Write a family agreement about staying alcohol- and drug-free.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 8 test on alcohol.

objectives: Analyze ads and media messages about alcohol and tobacco

days.title: Ad analysis
days.work: Analyze 3 alcohol or tobacco ads for target audience and hidden messages.

days.title: Movies and TV
days.work: Notice how alcohol or smoking is portrayed in a TV show or movie scene and whether consequences are shown.

days.title: Counter-ad
days.work: Create a counter-ad that shows the truth about a product.

days.title: Social media
days.work: Discuss influencers and sponsored posts that promote vaping.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a media literacy checklist for evaluating ads.

days.title: Types of pressure
days.work: Learn spoken, unspoken, positive and negative peer pressure with examples.

days.title: Scenario sort
days.work: Sort 10 scenario cards by type of pressure.

days.title: Good friends
days.work: Make a list of qualities of friends who support healthy choices.

days.title: Positive pressure
days.work: Plan a way to use positive peer pressure to encourage a healthy habit.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write about a time you resisted pressure or helped someone else.

days.title: Assertive voice
days.work: Compare passive, aggressive and assertive responses and practice an assertive voice and body language.

days.title: Refusal steps
days.work: Learn refusal strategies: say no clearly, give a reason, suggest an alternative, walk away.

days.title: Role-play 1
days.work: Role-play refusing a vape offered by an older kid.

days.title: Role-play 2
days.work: Role-play refusing alcohol at a party and leaving with help from a trusted adult.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Demonstrate refusal skills in a new scenario for a parent who scores the steps.

days.title: Decision model
days.work: Apply the decision model to 3 ATOD scenarios and write consequences.

days.title: Healthy alternatives
days.work: List 10 healthy activities to have fun and manage stress.

days.title: Pledge
days.work: Write a personal drug-free pledge and goal.

days.title: Share
days.work: Share your pledge with a trusted adult and discuss support.

days.title: Unit assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 9 test on influences, refusal and decisions.

objectives: Choose a health message and audience

days.title: Choose topic
days.work: Choose a topic: drink water, eat the rainbow, be active, or stay vape-free.

days.title: Audience
days.work: Identify the audience (family, neighbors, younger kids) and what message will reach them.

days.title: Facts
days.work: Gather 5 facts from reliable sources for the campaign.

days.title: Plan products
days.work: Plan 2 campaign products (poster, short video, flyer, skit).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Get feedback from a parent on the campaign plan.

days.title: Slogan
days.work: Write a catchy slogan and key message.

days.title: Poster
days.work: Create a poster with facts and visuals.

days.title: Video or skit
days.work: Record a 1-minute video or rehearse a skit.

days.title: Fact check
days.work: Check all facts against reliable sources.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Revise materials based on feedback.

weeks.topic: Presenting the campaign and year review

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the campaign to family or a community group.

days.title: Display
days.work: Display posters in a visible place (with permission).

days.title: Year review
days.work: Review nutrition, activity and ATOD key ideas with a game.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Take the end-of-year health assessment.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on your health goals and set a goal for summer.
